primary_number: 12.30% (2022), 13.60% (2023) — Mercer Marsh Benefits (MMB) market-wide Indonesia medical trend rates. The 26.5%/20.48% figures are retiree-cohort-specific from a single state-owned oil & gas employer, not general market medical cost inflation.
publisher: Narra J (peer-reviewed journal, PubMed Central) — Prastyo & Gani (2025). The paper internally cites Mercer Marsh Benefits (MMB) as the 12.30%/13.60% market-wide benchmark.
methodology_note: The PMC article (published May 8, 2025) is a retrospective cohort study of 29,695 retirees' healthcare claims from a single Indonesian state-owned oil and gas company (2020–2023). It reports 26.50% inflation (2022) and 20.48% (2023) for that specific retiree population, which the authors explicitly contrast against the MMB market-wide Indonesia figure of 12.30% (2022) and 13.60% (2023). The 26.5%/20.48% figures reflect a narrow, unrepresentative employer cohort — retirees of a single oil/gas SOE — not the Indonesian employer-sponsored health insurance market at large. The MMB figures (12.30%/13.60%) are the firm-imprint, insurer-survey-based market-wide numbers. BPS (Indonesia Central Bureau of Statistics) general CPI inflation for reference: 5.51% (2022) and 2.61% (2023).

recommended_edit_to_canonical: REPLACE the claim as currently written. The 26.5% (2022) and 20.48% (2023) figures represent retiree-cohort medical inflation for a single Indonesian state-owned oil & gas employer — they are NOT general market medical cost inflation rates. Using them to justify broad 'employer benefit envelope erosion' across Indonesia is methodologically unsound. RECOMMENDED REPLACEMENT: 'Medical cost inflation in Indonesia reached 12.3% in 2022 and 13.6% in 2023 per Mercer Marsh Benefits (MMB) Global Medical Trends Survey — more than double general CPI inflation of 5.5% (2022) and 2.6% (2023) — placing Indonesia among the highest medical trend markets in Asia.' Source: MMB Health Trends 2023 (firm-imprint, insurer survey of 226 carriers), corroborated by Jakarta Daily reporting (https://www.jakartadaily.id/health/1628177918/health-costs-in-indonesia-projected-to-increase-by-136-percent-higher-than-inflation). If the 26.5%/20.48% retiree-cohort figures are retained for any purpose, they must be clearly labelled as 'retiree-only cohort, single state-owned oil & gas employer, Prastyo & Gani (2025), Narra J' and must NOT be presented as general market medical cost inflation.
